script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 11. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
The iron in your blood.  The copper in your wires.  The gold in your jewelry.

Stars are fusion reactors—crushing hydrogen into helium, then into carbon, oxygen, and heavier elements. But fusion stops at iron. Creating heavier elements requires the violence of a supernova—the explosive death of a massive star. Gold, platinum, and other heavy elements require even more extreme conditions—neutron star collisions.  Two dead stars spiraling together and smashing create these precious metals.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You are the universe experiencing itself.  The atoms in your body traveled through stars and space to become you.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Cosmic Connection - Feel Your Stardust.

Here's your activity: Look at your hands. The atoms in them were forged in stars that died before our sun was born. Spend one minute feeling this cosmic connection—you are the universe organized into a person, briefly. What does this awareness change? This helps you experience visceral connection to cosmic origins.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about where metals come from can be applied to cosmic connection - feel your stardust. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
